source_status: STATUTORY CURRICULUM (schools must have regard to it; the subjects are compulsory)
in_force: 1 September 2026 (per the GOV.UK publication this PDF was downloaded from; the document body carries no commencement date)
requirement_text_verbatim: That people should be respectful in online interactions, and that the same principles apply to online relationships as to face-to-face relationships, including where people are anonymous. For example, the importance of avoiding putting pressure on others to share information and images online, and strategies for resisting peer pressure.
evidence_in_the_lessons: ks1-02 s9 teaches 'On screens we use the same kind words we use in the classroom. Screen words are still real words and they can still hurt.' ks2-07 s12 runs a group chat scenario that applies direct pressure to send a photo ('nearly everyone has done it, just waiting on YOU'). ks2-08 teaches bystander behaviour in a pile on.
what_is_missing: Anonymity is never named. The guidance requires pupils to know the same principles apply 'including where people are anonymous'. The word anonymous does not appear in any primary module.

For example, that people sometimes behave differently online, including pretending to be someone else, or pretending to be a child, and that this can lead to dangerous situations. How to recognise harmful content or harmful contact, and how to report this.
evidence_in_the_lessons: ks1-03 teaches sorting pictures into real, pretend and computer made, with a detective question said aloud before believing a picture. ks2-07 s12 shows a group chat with '2 you have never met'. ks2-08 teaches recognising harmful contact and the three moves ending in tell someone who can help.
what_is_missing: The specific worked example in the guidance, that adults sometimes pretend to be children online and that this can lead to dangerous situations, is not taught anywhere at primary.

in_force: 1 September 2026 (per the GOV.UK publication this PDF was downloaded from; the document body carries no commencement date)
requirement_text_verbatim: That keeping or forwarding indecent or sexual images of someone under 18 is a crime, even if the photo is of themselves or of someone who has consented, and even if the image was created by the child and/or using AI generated imagery. Pupils should understand the potentially serious consequences of acquiring or generating indecent or sexual images of someone under 18, including the potential for criminal charges and severe penalties including imprisonment. Pupils should know how to seek support and should understand that they will not be in trouble for asking for help, either at school or with the police, if an image of themselves has been shared. Pupils should also understand that sharing indecent images of people over 18 without consent is a crime.
evidence_in_the_lessons: ks4-16 teaches that the law applies to any image of a person under 18, teaches Report Remove, and teaches that a pupil will not be in trouble for asking for help.
what_is_missing: Two clauses the July 2025 guidance adds are not evidenced in the lesson text: that the offence applies to imagery created using AI, and that sharing indecent images of people over 18 without consent is also a crime. Both should be checked slide by slide before the module is claimed as full coverage.
